Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria, mild suprapubic cramps, and one episode of microscopic/macroscopic hematuria; no systemic symptoms. Clinical impression: uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection; empiric 3-day oral antibiotics prescribed.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain on urination for “a few days.”  
• Timeline: Began ≈3 days ago; persistent; no notable progression in severity.  
• Character: Stinging dysuria; occasional mild cramp-like lower abdominal pain during micturition.  
• Associated/ROS: One episode of small amount of blood in urine earlier today; malodorous urine. Denies urinary frequency, urgency, flank/back pain, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, vaginal discharge. Bowel habits normal; no diarrhoea.  
• Gynecologic/Sexual: Sexually active with one boyfriend (2 months); uses condoms. Last menstrual period “couple of weeks” ago (~3 weeks per physician recap). Never had prior STI screen. Thinks pregnancy unlikely.  
• Pertinent negatives: No fever, no loin pain, no vomiting, no diarrhoea.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – details not elaborated.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• None regularly.  
• Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate (dose/route/frequency not documented) without relief.  

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – causes swelling (suggestive of angioedema).

Social History:
• Lives with friends in a flat near college; second-year biology student.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Drinks alcohol socially on weekends.  
• Sexually active as above.

Family History:
• No known family history of kidney, bladder, or bowel disorders.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General/abdomen/urinary: Not recorded (telehealth consultation).

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered at this visit.  
• Physician advised pregnancy test if concern arises.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) most consistent with history; no red-flag features for pyelonephritis or alternative pathology at present.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute cystitis (UTI) – Supported by dysuria, hematuria, lower abdominal discomfort; lack of systemic features opposes more serious disease.  
2. Early pyelonephritis – Consider if develops fever, flank pain, or systemic illness (currently absent).  
(DDx list consistent; no conflicts noted.)

Issue 1: Dysuria / Suspected Acute Cystitis  
• Assessment: Likely uncomplicated UTI.  
• Plan:  
  – Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim 1 tablet PO twice daily for 3 days (exact agent to be supplied; dose/route/frequency per standard regimen).  
  – Hydration advice: Increase oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
  – Symptom monitoring: Return/call if no improvement by end of week or if develops fever, back/flank pain, or feels generally unwell (possible escalation to pyelonephritis).  
  – Avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
  – Urine culture not obtained; consider if recurrent or persisting.  

Issue 2: Pregnancy exclusion  
• Assessment: Low suspicion but not formally ruled out.  
• Plan: Advise home pregnancy test if any doubt or if symptoms persist/worsen.

Issue 3: STI screening / Health maintenance  
• Assessment: Never previously screened; sexually active.  
• Plan: Offer/arrange routine chlamydia & gonorrhoea screen at next opportunity; counsel on regular STI screening.

General plan items  
• Medication allergy documented; avoid clindamycin.  
• Encourage follow-up if new or worsening symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing clinical elements: No vitals or physical exam recorded; no urinalysis or culture ordered (may be expected but not performed).  
● No conflicts between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational noise, no inaudible segments affecting data extraction.
